newsitem.title: USA: Investors Insurance unsure about note.
newsitem.headline: Investors Insurance unsure about note.

text.p: Investors Insurance Group said Monday it was unsure whether or not it can settle an $8.0 million note on March 31, when the obligation is scheduled to be retired.

The note was issued in connection with the company's purchase of IIC Inc and its subsidiary, Investors Insurance Corp, from New Era Life Insurance Co in early in 1996. The note is secured by shares of IIC, it said.
It added it believes that the balance on the note is overstated because certain warranties made by the seller were false.

The company said that, after the purchase, the seller attempted to transfer the note to another insurance company. Both insurance companies then went into rehabilitation and both claim ownership of the note, it said.

At this time, it said it cannot negotiate an appropriate adjustment to the note because of the ownership issue. It expects the ownership of the note to be settled soon and to begin negotiations on the amount of the reductions.
While it plans to raise the capital needed to settle the note, it said there can be no assurance it will succeed in its efforts.
